newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil markets moribund, straight-run health.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil markets moribund, straight-run health.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were moribund on Monday, with traders searching for something to bring excitement to otherwise boring business.
Only one high sulphur fuel barge was heard traded, at $82 fob ARA. Bids and offers slipped back $1 from Friday's levels to $81/$82.

"It is very, very thin. Bunker demand is the poor one again," said one trader. He held out little hope for much improvement with the week due to be interrupted by May Day and a local holiday on Wednesday in Holland.
High and low sulphur cargoes were little discussed, though a British major was heard to be marketing a good quality, high sulphur cargo out of northern France.
News of a low sulphur straight-run cargo deal on Friday confirmed the grade's return to relative health.
Some 25,000 tonnes of 0.4 percent sulphur straight-run went from Britain to a Scandinavian buyer, loading first half May, for a price heard to be around $101 fob a tonne.
